interpretation.summary: An aggressive and heavily processed drum machine pattern, characteristic of industrial or EBM genres. It features a driving four-on-the-floor kick, a powerful gated reverb snare, and various hi-hat and percussive layers that build in complexity over the track's duration.

vocabulary.timbre: Classic electronic drum machine sounds—a boomy kick, a noisy snare drenched in gated reverb, and metallic hi-hats. The overall sound is sharp, processed, and synthetic rather than acoustic.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright, driven by the sharp crack of the snare and the persistent sizzle of metallic hi-hats. The high-frequency content from the cymbals and snare noise is a defining feature.
vocabulary.envelope: Extremely percussive and tight. The kick has a fast attack and short decay. The snare has an explosive, near-instantaneous attack followed by a very short, abrupt decay, characteristic of a gated reverb effect. Hi-hats are very short and sharp.
vocabulary.register_density: Starts with a sparse kick-snare pattern, then progressively layers hi-hats and other percussion, building density. The arrangement is anchored in the low register (kick) and high-mid/high register (snare, hats), leaving the midrange relatively open.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Unpitched percussion. The track is defined by rhythm and timbre, not harmony or melody.
vocabulary.groove: A driving, motorik four-on-the-floor groove at 120 BPM. The kick lands squarely on each beat, with a powerful backbeat snare on 2 and 4. Layered 8th and 16th note hi-hat patterns provide forward momentum and energy.
vocabulary.space_grit: Significant processing defines the sound. The snare features a prominent, large-sounding gated reverb, creating a sense of explosive but controlled space. There is a noticeable layer of saturation or light distortion across the kit, giving it a gritty, industrial texture.

tracks.name: Industrial Kick
tracks.pattern: A relentless and driving four-on-the-floor 1/4 note pattern.
tracks.description: The foundation of the track, providing a constant, powerful pulse from the very beginning. The sound is a deep, slightly boomy electronic kick with a sharp attack.

tracks.name: Gated Snare
tracks.instrument: A NoiseSynth processed with a very short reverb or a dedicated Gated Reverb effect.
tracks.pattern: A powerful, unwavering backbeat on counts 2 and 4.
tracks.description: The most character-defining element. Its explosive, reverberant, yet abruptly cut-off sound gives the track its classic 80s industrial feel. It is present almost throughout.

tracks.name: 8th Note Hi-Hat
tracks.pattern: A constant, machine-like 8th note pattern.
tracks.description: Enters after the initial kick/snare intro, providing the main high-frequency energy and driving the rhythm forward. Its metallic and consistent nature adds to the industrial feel.

tracks.name: Off-beat Open Hat
tracks.pattern: Syncopated off-beat hits, typically on the '+' of each quarter note, creating a classic disco/EBM feel.
tracks.description: This track adds a 'breathing' quality and syncopation to the otherwise rigid groove. Its longer decay contrasts with the tight closed hat.

tracks.name: Digital Clap/Rim
tracks.pattern: Syncopated 16th-note accent patterns that evolve throughout the track.
tracks.description: A dry, sharp percussive layer that adds rhythmic complexity and density, particularly in the track's middle and later sections. It sounds like a digital clap or a sharp rimshot.

interpretation.summary: A dynamic and atmospheric track featuring a lone, raspy male baritone vocal that builds with layered, choral harmonies and a wild, expressive saxophone solo, all drenched in heavy reverb.

vocabulary.timbre: A raspy male baritone voice is the primary element, joined by multi-tracked choral textures in the choruses and a reedy, wailing saxophone during the solo. The overall signal is highly tonal and harmonic.
vocabulary.brightness: The lead vocal is moderately bright and clear (mean centroid ~2.8kHz), cutting through well. The saxophone solo is even brighter and more aggressive in the upper-mid frequencies.
vocabulary.envelope: Vocal phrases have defined, sharp attacks and sustained notes. The choir harmonies have a softer, more pad-like envelope with slow attacks and long releases. The saxophone has a breathy attack with expressive dynamic swells.
vocabulary.register_density: The verses are sparse, featuring a single vocal line in the baritone register. Density increases dramatically in the choruses with layered harmonies and during the fast, note-dense saxophone solo.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: The track is firmly in a dark E minor. Vocal melodies and chorus harmonies (e.g., iv-III progressions like Am-G) reinforce this moody tonality. The saxophone solo incorporates notes from the E blues scale.
vocabulary.groove: The vocal delivery alternates between a rhythmic, almost spoken-word declamation in the verses and more sustained, melodic singing in the choruses. The saxophone solo consists of fast, flowing, and rhythmically complex phrases.
vocabulary.space_grit: A significant amount of reverb creates a large, cavernous space around all elements. The chorus vocals are stereo-widened and feel even more distant. The vocal and sax have a natural, acoustic grit rather than heavy electronic distortion.

tracks.name: Declamatory Lead Vocal
tracks.pattern: Rhythmic, spoken-word-like phrases in verses, transitioning to longer, sustained melodic lines in choruses. Features multi-tracked harmonies in chorus sections.
tracks.description: The central narrative element of the track, present from the beginning. It delivers the lyrics with a mix of rhythmic precision and melodic contour. In choruses, it's supported by wide, reverb-heavy harmonies. The synth approximation aims for the baritone weight and raspy character.

tracks.name: Wailing Sax Solo
tracks.pattern: A fast, virtuosic, and blues-inflected melodic solo with rapid runs, long-held notes, and expressive bends, occurring in the latter half of the track.
tracks.description: Takes over the lead role from the vocal for an extended instrumental section (approx. 2:03-2:35). The part is wild and expressive, full of fast passages and screaming high notes. The synth patch aims to capture the reedy bite and resonant quality of a saxophone.

interpretation.score_draft: speculative_starter: The piece is defined by a lead vocal and a sax solo. For the vocal, use a MonoSynth with a 'fatsawtooth' oscillator (count: 4, spread: 30) to create a thick baritone sound. Apply a low-pass filter around 2500Hz with a Q of 1.5, and add a touch of 'drive' (0.1) for warmth. Use a heavy 'reverbSend' (0.6). A sample phrase is ['B3', 'B3', 'B3', 'G3', 'E3', '', 'E3', '']. For the wailing sax solo, use another MonoSynth with a 'sawtooth' oscillator. Set a higher filter cutoff (~4000Hz) with more resonance (Q: 2.5) and more 'drive' (0.3) to get the reedy bite. A fast, bluesy 16th note line like ['E5', 'G5', 'A5', 'A#5', 'B5', 'A#5', 'A5', 'G5'] would be a good starting point. Both instruments need significant reverb to match the spaciousness of the original.

interpretation.summary: A dense and dramatic synth-driven piece in the post-punk/goth style. It is built on three primary layers: a frantic, continuous 16th-note sawtooth lead melody; a vast, slow-moving atmospheric pad that provides a harmonic wash; and powerful, heavily overdriven chord stabs that enter to create immense, climactic walls of sound. The entire mix is saturated in a large, cavernous reverb, giving it an epic and melancholic feel.

vocabulary.timbre: A blend of thick, analog-style synth textures, including a sharp, detuned sawtooth lead, a broad, evolving pad, and heavily overdriven, square-wave-based chord stabs.
vocabulary.brightness: Wide dynamic range in brightness, from dark, heavily filtered pads (~1200Hz) to piercing, resonant leads and distorted chords that can reach up to 5000Hz.
vocabulary.envelope: Diverse envelopes define the layers: fast attack/release for the frantic lead arpeggios, very slow attack (~2s) and long release (~5s) for the atmospheric pads, and a sharper percussive attack with a long decay for the overdriven power chords.
vocabulary.register_density: Primarily mid-to-high register. The track builds from sparse melodic lines to extremely dense textures with multiple layers of pads, leads, and chords occupying a wide frequency spectrum from E3 to B5.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Firmly in E minor, creating a dark, melancholic, and dramatic atmosphere. Harmony is built from simple minor and major chords within the key (e.g., Em, C, G), often voiced as powerful, open fifths in the aggressive sections.
vocabulary.groove: The groove is entirely synth-driven, defined by the relentless, propulsive 16th-note lead melody against a backdrop of slow-moving pads and powerful, rhythmic quarter-note chord stabs in the louder sections.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is drenched in a large, cavernous reverb space, giving it a grand, epic quality. Significant grit is applied, especially to the lead and chord synths, through distortion/drive, adding a raw, aggressive, post-punk edge.

tracks.name: Goth Lead Synth
tracks.pattern: Continuous, driving 16th-note melody outlining chord tones. It has a two-bar phrase structure that repeats with variations, creating a frantic and relentless feel.
tracks.description: The main melodic driver of the track, entering at 0:16. It's bright, slightly distorted, and sits front and center in the mix. It has a noticeable amount of reverb and a slight portamento between notes.

tracks.name: Cathedral Pad
tracks.pattern: Sustained whole-note or half-note chords, typically playing minor triads or open fifths. The harmonic rhythm is very slow, with chords held for one or two bars.
tracks.description: Provides the atmospheric, harmonic foundation. It's present throughout most of the track, swelling and receding. It starts smooth but becomes much louder, brighter, and more distorted around 1:40, creating a massive wall of sound. It's very wide and washed in reverb.

tracks.name: Overdriven Chords
tracks.pattern: Rhythmic power chord stabs, often landing on downbeats or playing a simple quarter-note pattern. Provides rhythmic weight and aggression.
tracks.description: This powerful layer enters in the more intense sections (e.g., 1:40) to create a climactic, industrial-tinged texture. It's a thick, heavily distorted synth playing simple chords, layered on top of the pad but with a much sharper attack and more grit.

interpretation.summary: A driving, motorik-style synth bass track that forms the relentless rhythmic and harmonic foundation of the song. A single, gritty monophonic synth plays a continuous stream of eighth notes, outlining E minor arpeggios and scale fragments. The timbre is that of a sawtooth wave passed through a resonant low-pass filter and a distortion/drive effect, giving it a dark, buzzy, and powerful character. The sound is direct and upfront, with a tight, percussive envelope and very little spatial effect.

vocabulary.timbre: A tonal, harmonically rich sawtooth-like waveform with significant saturation. Spectral flatness is near zero, indicating a pure synth tone rather than noise, with a high harmonic ratio confirming its tonal nature.
vocabulary.brightness: Dark and focused in the low-end. The spectral centroid is low (382 Hz), and a steep spectral rolloff at 611 Hz indicates a low-pass filter is aggressively shaping the sound, removing high-frequency content while retaining some buzzy upper-mid harmonics from distortion.
vocabulary.envelope: A tight and percussive envelope with a fast attack, quick decay, and low sustain. This creates a series of distinct, semi-plucked notes rather than a continuous drone, emphasizing the rhythmic drive.
vocabulary.register_density: The track is densely packed with a continuous stream of eighth notes, occupying the bass register (E1-E3). The density is consistent throughout, creating a hypnotic, machine-like pulse.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Rooted firmly in E minor, as suggested by the ground truth. The bassline primarily uses notes from the E natural minor scale (E, F#, G, A, B, C, D), often played as arpeggios (E-G-B) or stepwise motion, creating a dark, modal, and repetitive harmonic bed.
vocabulary.groove: A relentless, driving motorik groove based on a constant eighth-note pulse at 120 BPM. The feel is machine-like and hypnotic, with very little swing or dynamic variation in the performance, acting as the engine for the entire piece.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is gritty and direct, with a high degree of audible saturation or drive. There is minimal spatial processing; the track feels dry and close, with little to no reverb or significant delay, focusing all its energy on the raw, distorted tone.

tracks.name: Motorik Bass
tracks.pattern: 16-bar bass form in driving straight 8th-notes: a 4-bar chromatic descending pedal phrase (E->D->C#->C, connecting Em(i) to C(VI)) played 3x, then a 4-bar answer phrase that dips to A and climbs back A->B->C->D. Each root is pedaled, and the last 8th of most bars anticipates the next root (pickup) ahead of the bar line.
tracks.description: The harmonic + rhythmic engine: a chromatic descending pedal bass with an antecedent/consequent shape (3 descending statements + 1 dip-and-rise answer). Anticipation pickups pull each change ahead of the downbeat. (Hand-transcribed by ear; replaces the model's 1-bar arpeggio guess.)

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: Use a Tone.MonoSynth. Set the oscillator to 'sawtooth'. The envelope should be percussive: { attack: 0.01, decay: 0.2, sustain: 0.1, release: 0.2 }. Use a 'lowpass' filter with a cutoff around 800 Hz and a resonance (Q) of 2 to add character. The key ingredient is grit: set the synth's `drive` to around 0.5. Sequence a continuous 8th-note pattern in E minor, like ['E2', 'G2', 'B2', 'G2', 'A2', 'G2', 'F#2', 'E2'], to capture the motorik feel.

overview.summary: A driving, darkwave track featuring a relentless 16th-note bassline, raw analog synth textures, and cavernous reverb-drenched vocals, built on a stomping four-on-the-floor drum machine groove.

vocabulary.timbre: Dominated by raw, distorted analog-style synth sounds, including sawtooth bass, square wave chords, and noisy percussive elements, contrasted with a deep, baritone vocal.
vocabulary.brightness: Balanced but leaning dark, with a thick, murky low-mid range from the bass and chords, punctuated by the sharp, cutting quality of the lead synth arpeggios and metallic hi-hats.
vocabulary.envelope: A study in contrasts: the rhythm section (bass, drums) is extremely tight and percussive (short attack/decay), while vocals and lead synths are washed in long reverb, creating a vast sense of space.
vocabulary.register_density: Dense and layered. A constant, busy low-end from the bass, a solid mid-range foundation from chords and vocals, and an active high register occupied by the main synth riff and hi-hats.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: A clear F-sharp minor tonality, characterized by a dark, brooding mood. The progressions are simple and powerful, often moving between the tonic (F#m) and chords like Bm and C#m, reinforcing the track's somber feel.
vocabulary.groove: A rigid, motorik 120 BPM groove defined by a four-on-the-floor kick drum and a relentless 16th-note bassline, creating an insistent, danceable pulse reminiscent of EBM and post-punk.
vocabulary.space_grit: High grit and cavernous space. The bass and rhythm synths are heavily saturated with distortion ('drive'). This dry, gritty core is set against the immense space created by heavy, long-decay reverb on the lead synths and vocals.

tracks.name: Kick Drum
tracks.pattern: A classic, driving four-on-the-floor pattern on every quarter note.
tracks.description: The unchanging heartbeat of the track, providing a solid foundation from start to finish.

tracks.name: Snare Drum
tracks.pattern: A sharp backbeat on counts 2 and 4.
tracks.description: Provides the main backbeat, cutting through the mix with a burst of white noise.

tracks.name: Hi-Hats
tracks.pattern: Constant 16th-note pattern, creating a simmering, high-frequency energy.
tracks.description: A metallic, machine-like hi-hat pattern that drives the rhythm forward relentlessly.

tracks.name: Driving Bass
tracks.pattern: A relentless, non-stop 16th-note pattern playing the root of the current chord.
tracks.description: The central driving force of the entire song. Its distorted, pulsating line is the primary rhythmic and harmonic anchor. Enters at the very beginning and rarely stops.

tracks.name: Arp Lead
tracks.pattern: An iconic, arpeggiated 8th-note melody that outlines the chord changes.
tracks.description: The main melodic hook of the track, appearing in the intro and instrumental breaks. It has a wide, spacious sound due to chorus and heavy reverb.

tracks.name: Fuzz Chords
tracks.pattern: Sustained, heavily distorted power chords that add weight and texture to the chorus sections.
tracks.description: Enters during the main vocal sections ('mind is deconstructing') to create a wall of sound, thickening the harmony and adding aggression.

tracks.name: Solo Screech Synth
tracks.pattern: A chaotic, high-register melodic solo with fast runs and expressive pitch bends.
tracks.description: Appears in the latter half of the song (from approx 2:40) as a wild, guitar-like solo, adding a burst of chaotic energy.
